# Feature: Exclude dev + remote-tracking refs from guard diff

**Parent:** WL-0MV5MYBKJ0033P8U (Finish-gate live-repo guard trips on concurrent dev ref movement in multi-agent repos)
**Issue type:** feature (implementation slice)

## Summary

Helper-only change in `skill/shared/git_sandbox.py`: `diff_snapshots` and `fingerprint` ignore the `refs/heads/dev` ref and the whole `refs/remotes/origin/*` namespace, so concurrent movement of these refs by sibling agents (finish fast-forwards on the shared main checkout, concurrent fetch/push) can no longer fail the live-repo mutation guard. Because both consumers (F4 outer `run_tests.py:guarded_run_all`, F5 inner `skill/shared/live_repo_guard.py`) share the helper, neither needs a code change and they cannot drift.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC1 — `diff_snapshots` and `fingerprint` both report no change when only `refs/heads/dev` and/or `refs/remotes/origin/*` refs moved (movement or churn inside those namespaces is invisible).
- [ ] AC2 — Every other ref addition/removal/movement (e.g. fixture-branch creation like the incident's `feature-x` / `wl-*-test`), every local-config rewrite outside excluded branches, and every working-tree change still reports `changed == true` and fails the guard.
- [ ] AC3 — Existing exclusions are behaviour-preserving: `refs/worklog/*`, agent-worktree branch refs plus their `branch.<name>.*` config, and main-checkout anchoring all behave as before (existing regression tests stay green).
- [ ] AC4 — Helper-only: no consumer code change in `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` or `skill/shared/live_repo_guard.py`; the F1 guard-level regression tests (inner + outer) pass via the shared helper.
- [ ] AC5 — Exclusion is expressed as ref-namespace constants (`refs/remotes/origin/` prefix, `refs/heads/dev` exact) — never a `wl-*` name pattern; snapshots stay read-only plumbing; the per-test `fingerprint` stays cheap (no `status` scan).
- [ ] AC6 — The full project test suite (pytest + node, as declared by the test skill) passes with the change.

## Target outcome

`implement.py finish` and `/skill:test` stay green on a shared multi-agent host while siblings move `dev`/`origin/*`; genuine in-place checkout mutation (the SA-0MUIA3OE40001QJX `GIT_DIR`-leak class) still fails the gate.

## Definition of done (pass/fail)

- F1 helper + guard tests pass.
- Adversary tests still fail on genuine mutations.
- Full suite green.

## Minimal Implementation

- Add module constants (e.g. `CONCURRENCY_EXCLUDED_REF_NAMESPACES = ("refs/remotes/origin/",)` and `CONCURRENCY_EXCLUDED_REF_EXACT = "refs/heads/dev"`) plus one shared predicate `_is_concurrency_excluded_ref(ref)`.
- Apply the predicate to the ref filter in `diff_snapshots` (alongside the existing `excluded` set) and to the ref tuple in `fingerprint`. Keep raw refs in the snapshot for diagnostics/`describe_diff`.
- Verify no `branch.dev.*` config exclusion is required (dev-tracking config is static and not churned by a ref fast-forward); add it only if a guard test demonstrates churn.
- Run F1: helper + guard tests flip red → green.

## Constraints

- `skill/shared/git_sandbox.py` stays stdlib-only and loadable by file location (no `sys.path` mutation).
- Exclusion derived from git plumbing/ref-namespace constants, never a `wl-*` name pattern.
- The fix must not silently disable detection of the SA-0MUIA3OE40001QJX leak class (AC2; config + working-tree + non-excluded ref surfaces still fire).

## Key Files

- `skill/shared/git_sandbox.py`

## Dependencies

- The F1 regression-tests item — this implementation turns F1's red tests green (test-first ordering).

## Deliverables

- `git_sandbox.py` exclusion change; F1 regression tests green.
data.title: Exclude dev + remote-tracking refs from guard diff

# Feature: Document excluded refs contract and residual risk

**Parent:** WL-0MV5MYBKJ0033P8U (Finish-gate live-repo guard trips on concurrent dev ref movement in multi-agent repos)
**Issue type:** docs

## Summary

Update `docs/dev/test-isolation.md` §8 and the `git_sandbox.py` module docstring so the exclusion contract names exactly which ref namespaces are excluded (now including `refs/heads/dev` and `refs/remotes/origin/*`), why concurrent-agent movement of those refs is indistinguishable from suite-caused movement, and what residual risk remains.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC1 — `docs/dev/test-isolation.md` §8 lists every excluded ref namespace (`refs/worklog/*`, agent-worktree refs, `refs/heads/dev`, `refs/remotes/origin/*`) with the rationale that concurrent collaborative movement of those refs cannot be distinguished from suite-caused movement (residual-risk note).
- [ ] AC2 — The `git_sandbox.py` module docstring states the same extended exclusion contract so the helper is self-documenting for both consumers.
- [ ] AC3 — Residual risks are documented: (i) a sibling agent's unregistered feature-branch move can still trip the gate; (ii) a `refs/heads/dev`-only movement is no longer a standalone incident signal — the leak class is still caught via config + working-tree + non-excluded ref surfaces (cross-reference §8.4 / §9 and SA-0MUIA3OE40001QJX).

## Target outcome

Maintainers can reason about the guard's blind spots; the two consumers cannot drift because the contract lives next to the single shared helper.

## Definition of done (pass/fail)

- §8 and docstring updated and cross-referenced; no code behaviour change.

## Minimal Implementation

- Extend the §8.1 surfaces list and add a residual-risk paragraph in §8 naming the two exclusions added for concurrency reasons.
- Update the module docstring's residual-risk paragraph to name the new exclusions and cross-reference §8.4/§9.

## Key Files

- `docs/dev/test-isolation.md`
- `skill/shared/git_sandbox.py` (docstring only)

## Dependencies

- The F2 implementation item — documents its exclusion contract.

## Deliverables

- Updated §8 and module docstring.

# F2: Strengthen observable-outcome assertions (test-first)

**Parent:** WL-0MV5RYKQD000L5LM
**Issue type:** task (test-first — assertions land before any removal)

## Goal

For every occurrence classified `migrate` in F1 whose behaviour is **not** already proven by an
existing observable-outcome assertion, add the outcome assertion **first** (TDD ordering), so F3
can remove the internal/redundant call-shape assertion without weakening regression coverage.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Coverage gaps closed** — each `migrate` occurrence that F1 identified as lacking equivalent
  outcome coverage now has a new assertion on a returned value/state (e.g. `spawned`, `outcome`,
  poll result) that proves the same behaviour.
- **Observable only** — all new assertions assert observable results; none of them assert mock
  call shape via `toHaveBeenCalledWith`.
- **Count preserved** — the test-case count in `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.*.test.ts`
  is unchanged.
- **Scope confined** — only `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.*.test.ts` files (and inline
  comments) change; no production-code change; no new test dependencies.
- **Target suite green** — the target file's test suite passes (via the test skill) after the
  additions.

## Notes

- If F1 finds that **every** `migrate` occurrence already has equivalent outcome coverage (the
  4 `handle.once` wiring cases drive their listeners and assert `spawned`; redundant query rows
  assert `outcome.kind`/`outcome.candidate`), the deliverable is a short comment recording that
  no new assertions are required, and F3 proceeds with removal only. This satisfies the
  test-first requirement because the replacement assertions already exist in the same tests.

## Constraints

- Test-first: additions precede any removals in F3.
- UK English throughout.

**Key Files:**

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.pane.test.ts` — 4 `handle.once` wiring cases (lines ~100–150)
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.dispatch.test.ts` — redundant `getNextItem` query rows

## Deliverables

- New/changed observable-outcome assertions (or the no-op conclusion comment)
data.title: F2: Strengthen observable-outcome assertions (test-first)

# F3: Migrate internal/redundant assertions; annotate retained (toHaveBeenCalledWith)

**Parent:** WL-0MV5RYKQD000L5LM
**Issue type:** task (implementation — the migration itself)

## Goal

Convert every occurrence classified `migrate` in F1 so the same behaviour is asserted through an
observable outcome, or removed where an existing assertion in the same test already proves that
behaviour (F2/table). Add a short inline justification comment to every retained assertion
(parent AC3), so the remaining 100+ dependency-call assertions are auditable.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Migration complete** — every `migrate` occurrence is converted/removed per the F1 table,
  and the table names the outcome assertion that replaces each removed assertion.
- **Zero wiring assertions** — `rg 'handle\.once\)\.toHaveBeenCalledWith' packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker*.test.ts`
  returns **zero** matches.
- **Retained justified** — every retained occurrence carries an inline comment stating why the
  dependency call is the unit's observable contract (producer Q2-A).
- **Coverage preserved** — no test case is deleted; the test-case count is unchanged; only
  assertions move/change form.
- **Scope confined** — only `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.*.test.ts` files change (plus
  inline comments); no production-code change; no new test dependencies.
- **Target suite green** — the affected test files pass (via the test skill) with the changes.

## Constraints

- Preserve test semantics: no assertion is dropped without a named replacement or an explicit
  table justification.
- Retained ordering assertions (`toHaveBeenNthCalledWith` proving tier/fallback order) stay
  unless an outcome assertion proves identical ordering.
- UK English throughout.

**Key Files:**

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.pane.test.ts` — migrate 4 `handle.once` wiring assertions
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.dispatch.test.ts` — migrate redundant query-call assertions
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.*.test.ts` (all 14 files) — annotate retained assertions inline

## Deliverables

- Edited test files with migrated assertions and inline justifications
- Zero `handle.once`-`toHaveBeenCalledWith` matches (rg verification)

# F4: Verify migration and close parent AC4 (toHaveBeenCalledWith)

**Parent:** WL-0MV5RYKQD000L5LM
**Issue type:** task (verification + parent evidence)

## Goal

Verify the migration end-to-end (parent AC4/AC6) and post the evidence comment on the split
parent WL-0MV28X3SL005R5KX closing deferred AC4 (parent AC5, producer Q3-A) — without reopening
or re-auditing that parent.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Behavioural coverage preserved (AC4)** — the test-case count per
  `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.*.test.ts` file is identical to the `b195e01a` baseline;
  a thin diff against the baseline commit shows only assertion/comment changes and no
  `it(`/`test(` lines deleted.
- **Scope confined** — `git diff` touches only `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.*.test.ts`
  files; no production-code change (verified via `--stat` against `b195e01a` or HEAD).
- **Zero wiring assertions (AC2)** — `rg 'handle\.once\)\.toHaveBeenCalledWith'` returns zero
  matches.
- **Docs and full suite (AC6)** — related documentation and code comments updated to reflect
  the migration; the full project test suite passes via `/skill:test`.
- **Parent AC4 evidence (AC5, Q3-A)** — an evidence comment is posted on WL-0MV28X3SL005R5KX
  linking WL-0MV5RYKQD000L5LM and its outcome; the parent is NOT reopened or re-audited
  (stays `completed`/`done`).
- **Classification reconciled** — the F1 comment's per-file category counts reconcile to the
  post-migration file state.

## Constraints

- Do not modify production code or non-downtime-worker test files.
- The parent (WL-0MV28X3SL005R5KX) stays `completed`/`done`.
- UK English throughout.

**Key Files:**

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.*.test.ts` (14 files, verification targets)
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.fixtures.ts` (read-only reference)
- `skill/shared/test-writing-guidelines.md` (reference; no change expected)

## Deliverables

- Evidence comment on WL-0MV28X3SL005R5KX (parent AC4 closed)

# End-to-end verification & full-suite gate

Final end-to-end verification that the restored flag + icon behave correctly across the whole stack, and that the full suite is green.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] E2E: an item with `needsProducerReview=true` renders ❌ in the herdr selection list and a `Producer Review` metadata row; `false` renders ✅; unset renders neither.
- [ ] E2E: flag-true items are excluded from downtime auto-dispatch; the review queue ranks them first (bucket 1).
- [ ] E2E: `wl reviewed <id> true` sets the flag; `--needs-producer-review` filters work; JSONL round-trip and cross-root sync of the flag work.
- [ ] Audit-safety regression: flipping the flag does not make a fresh audit stale (WL-0MSN6ZCTN0027U2R).
- [ ] Ship gate blocks release on a flag-true item (with F6's SA gate active).
- [ ] Full project test suite passes via `/skill:test`.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`, `packages/shared/src/icons.ts`, `src/commands/reviewed.ts`
- `tests/` (E2E coverage)

## Deliverables

Verified end-to-end restore with a green full suite.
